column1: Cartwright Oswin/s0|What part of the wheel failed?|The part that needs repair rather than another hopeful push. I am checking the fittings as well.|Could you move the load first?|Only if it makes the cart safer to handle. An unstable load can make a broken wheel worse.

Cartwright Oswin/s1|Why choose a wagon over a boat?|Father knew the roads better than the water. Neither forgives neglect.|Has the wagon served you well?|For years, with repairs. Familiar equipment still needs care.

Cartwright Oswin/e0|What failed that the peg could not fix?|A different part of the wheel. Carrying one spare never meant carrying a whole workshop.|Will you carry more spares now?|The sensible ones. The cart cannot become heavier every time something teaches me a lesson.

Cartwright Oswin/e1|What makes a tight corner difficult?|The wagon and load need more turning room than a walker.|Do you plan a route around them?|When carrying something awkward, yes. A shortcut is not useful if the cart cannot take it.

Cartwright Oswin/w0|Does the royal load always go first?|That is how the guards arrange it, regardless of who has waited longest.|What do delays cost you?|Spoiled schedules, provisions, sometimes goods that cannot wait in the weather.|Could carts be cleared more fairly?|By the obstruction and urgency, rather than the seal painted on a wagon.

Cartwright Oswin/w1|Who should decide whose repair is urgent?|People who can assess the danger and practical need, with the drivers heard.|Would you wait for someone worse off?|Yes. I object to rank jumping the line, not a genuine emergency.|Will the road still have delays?|Of course. Wheels will continue breaking without royal assistance.
Cartwright Oswin/r|Why check every pin twice?|Because a hurried final check can undo a careful repair.|Will you change the load?|I will keep it within what the repaired cart can safely carry.

Miner Marn/s0|Why is pulling first dangerous?|The cart may be supporting loose material. Disturbing it can bring more down.|Who decides the order of work?|The crew assessing the bank, with everyone clear about the plan.

Miner Marn/s1|Do you like carving badgers?|I have developed a fondness for them, given my apparent talent.|Would you try a different animal again?|Yes. I would like Nerik to recognise one without being told first.

Miner Marn/e0|Does it look like a bird to you?|Enough that I kept working on the beak rather than adding a badger's nose.|Will Nerik ever approve?|He enjoys the joke. I can improve the carving without waiting for his permission.

Miner Marn/e1|What do you do when someone hears movement?|Stop and assess it. Nobody needs to prove bravery by continuing under doubt.|Can stone fall without warning?|Yes. Listening is one precaution, not a guarantee.

Miner Marn/w0|Why can't the officials set a faster pace?|Because the bank's condition determines the safe work, not their impatience.|Does Nerik understand the risks?|He asks questions and listens. That makes him useful to work beside.|What do you tell someone demanding speed?|Which danger we are dealing with and why the step cannot be skipped.

Miner Marn/w1|Will your methods change now?|The stone still requires the same care. I hope the pressure to ignore that decreases.|Who should set the schedule?|Someone who has heard the crew's assessment, including the uncertain parts.|What if a delay costs money?|An injury costs more than a line in the shipment record can describe.

Miner Marn/r|Could the bank shift again?|Conditions can change. We checked it before reopening, not for all eternity.|Should carts go through slowly?|With room to manoeuvre and drivers paying attention, yes.

Miner Nerik/s0|Did you ignore Marn's warning?|I hoped the noise meant less than it did. That was not an inspection.|Can you recognise the sound now?|Better. I still ask when I am uncertain rather than pretending experience arrived overnight.

Miner Nerik/s1|Why buy a lamp first?|Mother used the old one every evening. I wanted my first wages to improve something she actually used.|Did you tell her it was a gift?|Very clearly, before she could suggest I spend the money on myself.

Miner Nerik/e0|Why defend the old lamp?|It had served her a long time. Accepting a better one did not make her ungrateful to it.|Does she thank you directly?|Sometimes. Seeing it used tells me plenty.

Miner Nerik/e1|Who usually chooses the first stone?|We assess it together, with Marn's experience given the weight it deserves.|What if you disagree?|We stop and explain why. Pulling while arguing would settle nothing safely.

Miner Nerik/w0|What do you do with a doubtful order?|Ask Marn and explain the concern before acting.|Is it hard to question an older worker?|Yes. It is still better than quietly doing something dangerous.|Has Marn ever changed a plan after your question?|When the question revealed something worth checking. Experience does not make inspection unnecessary.

Miner Nerik/w1|Would you help train a new miner?|Within what I know, and with experienced workers involved.|What lesson would you begin with?|Ask when uncertain, and pay attention when someone calls for a stop.|Will every order become sensible now?|No. We still need people able to question and correct them.

Miner Nerik/r|Why inspect an unchanged bank?|To confirm that moving the carts had not disturbed anything above.|Did you want to stop before checking?|Yes. Being nearly finished is precisely when I am tempted to hurry.

Snowbuilder Nessa/s0|Why give it your brother's scarf?|It made the figure recognisably his, at least to the family.|Were you pleased when he finally visited?|Very. The scarf was a much better reminder with its owner beside it.

Snowbuilder Nessa/s1|How do you give each face character?|A different tilt or shape, chosen before I fuss over tiny details.|Do you plan the whole family first?|Only roughly. The snow and the weather get a say.

Snowbuilder Nessa/e0|Does the hat stay put?|Usually. I check after wind rather than expect snow to hold it forever.|Why build a small figure too?|It makes the group feel like a family rather than a row of sentries.

Snowbuilder Nessa/e1|Do you repair them during a thaw?|Only while it makes sense. Eventually I collect the hats and let the snow go.|Will you build the same faces next winter?|Perhaps with changes. I can remember one winter without repeating it exactly.

Snowbuilder Nessa/h|Who taught you that family custom?|Older relatives who knew what a closed winter road felt like.|Does building a figure help with missing someone?|It gives the missing a small, affectionate task. It does not replace the visit.

Snowbuilder Nessa/w0|Did the patrols keep your brother away?|Unsafe roads and official demands added to the ordinary difficulties of winter.|Do the figures make you less lonely?|A little, especially when neighbours recognise whom I meant.|Would you rather have the real visitors?|Naturally. Snow is poor at helping with supper.

Snowbuilder Nessa/w1|Would your brother enjoy building one?|He will have plenty of opinions about its nose.|Will winter still close the roads?|Yes. One less reason to miss a visit is still worth being glad about.|Where will you build the figures?|Well clear of the route people need to use.

Snowbuilder Nessa/r|Why move the figures?|The road needs to serve travellers before it serves my decorations.|Will the little dog stay off the road?|Firmly. Its imaginary wanderings will not become another obstruction.
Orin/e0|Do you greet everyone who passes?|Anyone who looks willing to pause. I let hurried people be hurried.|Why watch arrivals?|A familiar face may bring news; a new one may need directions.
Orin/e1|Can a person's pace change?|Certainly. A familiar rhythm is a clue, not a name.|Do I really hurry that much?|Often enough to look as though the next thing has caught your interest.
Orin/h|Why weren't the planters recorded?|Ordinary work seldom seemed worth writing down at the time.|Can the remaining names still be saved?|Yes, by asking carefully while people remember them.

Orin/w0|What was my father like in the square?|Willing to ask a question. I remember the ease of those conversations as much as the answers.|Why would disagreement concern an officer?|Under this king, criticism is treated as a threat rather than ordinary speech.|Do people still gather?|They do, with more caution than such a familiar place should require.

Orin/w1|What feels restored about the square?|People can pause and speak without first judging every listener.|Would you like to hear about my journey?|What you want to tell. Sitting together need not become another duty.|Do you think Dad would have liked this?|I think he would have liked hearing you finish a thought without fear.

Weft/e0|Do you mend things for travellers?|Small repairs when I can. A camp blanket or torn cloth can make a miserable night worse.|What if the thread frays?|Trim and prepare it properly rather than force the damaged end through.

Weft/e1|How do you decide what to keep?|Whether a sound scrap suits a likely repair and there is room for it.|Do travellers appreciate small repairs?|Especially when the alternative is carrying the same tear down the road.

Weft/w0|Have travellers stopped using the camps?|Fewer linger when they fear being questioned on the road.|Why do patrols call that prosperity?|They count traffic serving their needs and ignore the empty beds beside it.|Could you lower the price?|Price is not the main reason people are afraid to stay.

Weft/w1|Would you welcome competition again?|Yes. Two busy camps are better than both wondering when the next traveller will arrive.|What would you improve first?|The things guests actually use to rest and eat comfortably.|Will safe travel return at once?|No. We still need reliable news about the routes and their remaining dangers.
Dorrick/e0|What keeps becoming the last job?|A repair or check I notice just as supper is ready.|Could it wait until afterwards?|Often. I am learning to distinguish urgent from merely visible.

Dorrick/e1|Can a repaired thing still fail?|Of course. I trust inspection and testing, not the fact that it has a patch.|Would you reject an unsafe repair?|Yes. Admiring effort does not make a weak joint sound.

Dorrick/w0|What worries you behind that door?|Conditions in the workings that deserve investigation before more men enter.|Have you explained that to the officers?|Yes. The instruction to open it has travelled more readily than the concern sent back.|What would a proper decision require?|A careful assessment by people who understand the galleries.

Dorrick/w1|Who should assess the galleries?|Experienced workers able to report hazards without being punished for delay.|Will you open every route now?|Only what can be made acceptably safe. Freedom does not strengthen damaged stone.|Why do shipment promises cause trouble?|They commit people to output before the work's actual limits are understood.
Hask/e0|Would you rather have some quiet?|I have had quiet. A little company is welcome.|What were you thinking about?|The usual people and chores. Nothing requiring us to whisper around it.

Hask/e1|What might a newcomer notice?|A changed doorway or view I have stopped examining.|Do you enjoy showing someone around?|When they are interested. A familiar place can become interesting again through their questions.

Hask/w0|Why are the young people leaving?|Work, fear, the hope of something better. Not every departure has one cause.|Do you want them all to stay?|I want them to have a real choice, and a reason to come back willingly.|What do the notices miss?|The households waiting for news from people the figures no longer count as here.

Hask/w1|Would a visit be enough for you?|I would be glad to see them without requiring them to rebuild their lives for my comfort.|Have you received news?|Sometimes. A short message can relieve a long stretch of wondering.|What would you tell someone returning?|That they are welcome, and may explain their journey in their own time.
Garrow/e0|Does putting tools away help the next job?|Yes. Stopping well makes beginning again easier.|What if a tool is damaged?|Set it aside clearly for repair, not back among things ready to use.

Garrow/e1|Do people often put things in the wrong place?|Enough that one question could save a later search.|What if you are busy when they ask?|A brief answer usually takes less time than correcting the guess.

Garrow/w0|How do you recognise an old promise?|The same promised relief follows a new demand, with the relief always somewhere ahead.|Have you ever believed one?|Yes. Experience is partly a record of things that persuaded us once.|What would convince you now?|Specific work carried out, with the people affected able to judge the result.

Garrow/w1|Did you think his rule would last forever?|Longer than I expected to be here. I am happy to correct the estimate.|What would you like to see next?|Ordinary improvements people can name without quoting a speech.|Will you still sit and watch?|Certainly. I have a better reason to be interested now.

Marek/e0|What usually interrupts the cup?|Work needing attention, or someone arriving with a question.|Would you like me to let you finish it?|We can talk while I sit. That would satisfy both ambitions.

Marek/e1|What helps you remember someone?|Their manner and the last conversation, more than the contents of a purchase.|What if you forget a name?|I ask. Pretending usually makes the eventual mistake larger.

Marek/w0|Are the royal loads secret?|Their purpose is often withheld from the people handling them.|Do you need to know every detail?|Enough to work responsibly and understand what we are being asked to support.|What do officials say when you ask?|That the seal should be explanation enough. It is not.

Marek/w1|What would a plain answer change?|It would let workers understand the task and raise relevant concerns.|Would you refuse a harmful load?|I would want the right to question it, rather than be told the question is disloyal.|Is openness enough by itself?|No. It makes the actual decision easier to examine.

Bregga/e0|What do you prepare first?|Things needed regularly when going outside becomes harder, without blocking safe movement indoors.|Do you wait for the first snowfall?|No. That would let the weather choose the working day.

Bregga/e1|Shall I come in or let you close it?|Choose whichever suits your visit. The warm air would appreciate a decision.|Do people often linger in doorways?|Usually while saying they will not keep me a moment.

Bregga/w0|Do the men take wood meant for winter?|They see a stack and call it available. We see the months it must last.|Could you cut more to replace it?|Not without time, labour and damage to the ground if too much is taken.|What would you tell an officer?|Count the household's winter needs before counting the wood as surplus.

Bregga/w1|How long does cut ground need?|It depends on the growth and conditions. It cannot be ordered into recovery.|Will you still gather winter fuel?|Carefully, with future seasons in mind as well as this one.|Why does refusing a levy matter so much?|It may let a household keep warmth it has already worked to provide.

Torvald/e0|What if the flame remains dim?|Check the lamp's condition and fuel. Clean glass is only one part.|Do you inspect the handle too?|Yes. The light must be carried safely as well as shine clearly.

Torvald/e1|What goes in the easiest pocket?|What I may need quickly and can safely carry there.|Do you check before entering darkness?|Always. Familiar placement is useful only if the item is actually present.

Torvald/w0|What support did miners give each other?|Checking equipment, sharing warnings and noticing who had not returned.|Did officials ignore missing men?|They were more eager for output than to hear what the workings cost.|What should a responsible order include?|The means and time to do the work safely, and concern when people do not return.

Torvald/w1|Where should the names be kept?|In records families can see and correct, not just a total in an account.|Will recording them help the families?|It cannot restore anyone. It can stop the loss being treated as an anonymous figure.|What else do those families need?|To be heard about their actual circumstances, rather than told a new tally settles everything.
Ingrid/e0|Do you check it more than once?|If there is a reason. Otherwise one careful check is enough.|What if it no longer closes well?|It needs repair before familiarity persuades me to ignore it.

Ingrid/e1|Do you check on a dark window?|If someone is expected home and the darkness is unusual, I may ask a neighbour.|Could the person simply be asleep?|Of course. A changed routine is a reason to check kindly, not assume disaster.

Ingrid/w0|Why turn someone back as a storm approached?|An officer followed a rule about passage without considering what the weather meant.|Did you bring them inside?|Yes. Getting warm mattered more than continuing the argument outdoors.|Could they continue later?|When conditions allowed. Being right about the patrol did not make the storm harmless.

Ingrid/w1|Will former strangers be welcome too?|Anyone needing a reasonable welcome, not only familiar faces.|Why did people arrive quietly before?|They feared drawing attention after trouble on the road.|Will winter still make arrivals difficult?|Yes. We can prepare for weather without adding suspicion to it.

Sigrun/e0|What do you wrap in the cloth?|Things that need staying dry, according to the journey. I keep the cloth protected until needed.|Do you dry it before packing again?|Certainly. A damp spare offers poor reassurance.

Sigrun/e1|Do you turn back in bad conditions?|When that is the sensible option. Reaching a destination is not worth every risk.|How do you judge the footing?|By what is actually underfoot, not how confidently the last traveller described it.

Sigrun/w0|What do those numbers tell you?|Whether people are safely housed, who has been lost, and what can be shared.|Do official notices count different things?|They count achievements that flatter the rule. Households notice whether supper is possible.|Which number would you like to improve?|The bowls I can fill without worrying who must go without tomorrow.

Sigrun/w1|What would cheerful growth look like?|Visitors staying for company and households making plans beyond getting through the winter.|Will the town need more supplies?|Of course. A hopeful future still requires sensible preparation.|What do you most want an ordinary year for?|People who have spent too many seasons expecting another loss.

Asta/e0|Would you sacrifice the view for comfort?|For a long conversation, yes. I can look at the view standing up first.|Do you stay in one place long?|When the company or work warrants it. That is why the seat matters.

Asta/e1|Does the subject matter?|Somewhat, but being heard can matter more than finding a remarkable story.|Can a short conversation do that?|Yes. Time alone does not measure whether someone paid attention.

Asta/w0|What changes when a patrol appears?|Voices soften, names disappear, and an ordinary subject suddenly ends.|Could people simply be finished talking?|Once, perhaps. A repeated pattern invites a more careful question.|Do you ask them why afterwards?|If they seem willing. I do not turn another person's caution into an examination.

Asta/w1|Are people happy to have their words recorded?|I ask. Speaking freely is not automatically agreeing to become a written example.|What are they talking about now?|Plans, complaints, disagreements that no longer stop at the sound of boots.|Will you include conflicting opinions?|Yes. A lively record should not flatten everyone into one convenient voice.
